scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO develops next-generation AI agents powered by large AI language models (LLMs) capable of interpreting instructions, generating plans, using tools, and performing actions autonomously to achieve complex real-world tasks.

Pillar 1 develops a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine combining LLM-based reasoning with symbolic planning methods (Monte Carlo Tree Search, hierarchical task networks) to decompose high-level goals into structured sub-task graphs with formally specified pre-conditions, post-conditions, verification checkpoints, and self-correction through plan monitoring.

Pillar 2 develops a unified adaptive memory architecture integrating working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory, governed by a memory controller that manages information flow across stores to sustain coherent long-horizon agent behaviour extending beyond any single LLM context window.

Pillar 3 develops decentralised multi-agent coordination protocols enabling heterogeneous agents to negotiate task assignments, establish shared commitments with provable convergence guarantees, resolve resource and plan conflicts, and produce auditable delegation and negotiation traces.

A cross-cutting External Tool and API Orchestration Layer provides a typed tool registry with capability models, formal tool selection and invocation policies integrated with the neuro-symbolic planning engine, standardised API adapters (including HL7 FHIR and OPC-UA), post-invocation verification and grounding, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and auditable tool execution traces — architecturally integrated across all three research pillars.

MAESTRO validates through a healthcare clinical decision support demonstrator (Apply AI sector: healthcare) co-designed with clinical partners, with quantitative KPIs including diagnostic accuracy, reasoning trace completeness, and tool invocation success rate benchmarked against clinician baselines.

MAESTRO validates through an advanced manufacturing process optimisation demonstrator (Apply AI sector: advanced manufacturing) co-designed with manufacturing partners, with quantitative KPIs including defect rate reduction, energy savings, and multi-agent coordination latency benchmarked against operational baselines.

MAESTRO validates through a logistics and supply chain demonstrator as a cross-sector transfer demonstrator explicitly framed as confirming architecture portability beyond the minimum sector requirement, co-designed with logistics industry partners across international supply chain corridors.

MAESTRO does not address in-vehicle autonomous driving as a full demonstrator sector; it provides only a targeted architectural mapping analysis (WP8) to assess transferability of the MAESTRO architecture to autonomous driving settings.
scope_findings.flag_reason: CC-10 establishes a portfolio coverage mechanism requiring that grants are awarded to ensure at least one funded proposal per each of the three specifically identified Apply AI sectors — healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and in-vehicle autonomous driving. MAESTRO covers healthcare and advanced manufacturing with full demonstrators but addresses in-vehicle autonomous driving only through an architectural mapping analysis (WP8), which falls short of a demonstrator. While SR-07 requires application in at least one Apply AI sector and MAESTRO satisfies this through two call-identified sectors, the architectural mapping analysis cannot be credited as demonstrator-level coverage of the in-vehicle autonomous driving sector for CC-10 portfolio purposes. The concept explicitly acknowledges this gap. Evaluators applying CC-10 portfolio logic may score proposals covering all three specified sectors more favourably; this borderline positioning requires explicit strategic acknowledgement in the proposal and cannot be confirmed as fully in-scope relative to CC-10.

scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO incorporates qualitative and quantitative KPIs, standardised benchmarking across all demonstrators, and structured progress monitoring at 6-month integration checkpoints.
Agent behaviour validation and monitoring techniques are incorporated as required design elements, with all demonstrators assessed through quantitative KPIs and validated in operational environments.

MAESTRO implements the co-programmed European Partnership on AI, Data and Robotics (ADRA) and allocates dedicated tasks for cohesion activities with both ADRA and the GenAI4EU central Hub (CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18).

All research outputs — frameworks, models, benchmarks, the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and demonstrator results — will be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
MAESTRO will link to the resources offered by AI Factories and Data Labs for compute-intensive training and evaluation.
Demonstrator results will be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities.
The requested EU contribution is €18,500,000.

MAESTRO's open-source framework, External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and standardised agent interaction protocols will lower barriers for European SMEs and startups to build on next-generation AI agent technology.
scope_findings.flag_reason: The claim that MAESTRO will release an open-source framework is not explicitly confirmed as required or expected by any scope element in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json. SR-10 and CC-05 require results to be shared through the AI-on-demand platform but do not specify open-source licensing or open-source distribution as the mandated or confirmed dissemination mode. Confirming this claim as in-scope from Tier 2B data alone would require inferring from generic programme knowledge about Horizon Europe open-access expectations, which is prohibited. The open-source assertion should be assessed against Tier 1 normative framework requirements for open science rather than treated as confirmed from Tier 2B scope elements.

scope_findings.claim: Demonstrator results will be disseminated via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).
scope_findings.flag_reason: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) are not mentioned as a dissemination channel in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json. CC-07 identifies AI Factories, Data Labs, and Testing and Experiment Facilities as the relevant infrastructure; SR-10 and CC-05 specify the AI-on-demand platform as the required sharing channel. EDIH dissemination is not prohibited by any constraint, but no Tier 2B scope element references EDIHs, and this claim cannot be confirmed as within scope from Tier 2B data alone without inferring from generic programme knowledge.

scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO strengthens the European AI ecosystem's competitiveness and reduces strategic dependency on non-European AI platforms.
scope_findings.flag_reason: The claim about strengthening European AI ecosystem competitiveness and reducing strategic dependency on non-European AI platforms is a broader policy impact assertion not explicitly confirmed by any scope element in scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json. No Tier 2B scope element addresses strategic autonomy, ecosystem competitiveness, or dependency reduction as a scope requirement or constraint. Confirming this claim as in-scope would require inferring from generic Horizon Europe programme knowledge about strategic autonomy policy objectives, which is prohibited by the constitutional constraint that scope boundary is defined by Tier 2B only.

scope_findings.claim: The strategic positioning states that demonstrators will be validated in operational environments at TRL 5; the starting TRL is not explicitly stated in the concept note or strategic positioning text.
scope_findings.flag_reason: CC-01 requires activities to start at TRL 2 and achieve TRL 5 by the end of the project. The strategic positioning confirms TRL 5 as the validation endpoint in operational environments, satisfying the TRL 5 endpoint requirement. However, the starting TRL of TRL 2 is not explicitly stated anywhere in the concept note or strategic positioning content evaluated here. The proposal must explicitly confirm TRL 2 as the starting point to demonstrate full compliance with CC-01; the absence of this statement is a traceability gap that must be resolved before the relevant proposal sections are finalised.
